comparisons.peer_topic: Series EE preferred stock dividend terms
comparisons.peer_summary: Series EE preferred stock, issued as depositary shares, pays quarterly fixed dividends until February 15, 2030, thereafter resetting every five years to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572%, with dividends payable only when declared by the Board.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citigroup (C) utilize depositary shares to represent fractional interests in their preferred stock series and employ a fixed-rate period followed by a reset tied to the five-year treasury rate. GS's Series Z is represented by 25 depositary shares and resets to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate after February 2030. Similarly, C's Series EE is represented by 1/25th depositary shares and resets to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572% after February 2030. While GS resets annually in semi-annual periods post-fixing, C resets quarterly every five years, showing a structural similarity in benchmarking but a difference in reset frequency.

sentences.text: Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

Dividends on Series Z Preferred Stock, if declared, are payable semi-annually at (i) 6.85% per annum from the issuance date to, but excluding, February 10, 2030 and, thereafter, (ii) 2.461% per annum plus the five-year treasury rate.
(16)Issued as depositary shares, each representing a 1/25th interest in a share of the corresponding series of non-cumulative perpetual preferred stock.

Dividends are payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 at a fixed rate until, but excluding, February 15, 2030, thereafter payable quarterly on the same dates at a fixed rate that resets on the Series EE reset date and every five years thereafter equal to the five-year treasury rate plus 2.572%, in each case when, as and if declared by the Citi Board of Directors.

comparisons.peer_topic: Issuance of Series OO preferred stock
comparisons.peer_summary: On February 4, 2025, JPMorgan issued $3.0 billion of fixed-rate reset non-cumulative preferred stock, Series OO.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and JPMorgan (JPM) disclosed the issuance of new fixed-rate reset non-cumulative preferred stock series in early 2025. GS issued Series Z shares in January 2025, while JPM issued Series OO shares in February 2025. Both issuances represent strategic capital raises using similar instrument structures (non-cumulative preferred stock with reset rates), although the text for JPM only specifies the total dollar amount ($3.0 billion) and issuance date, whereas GS provides share counts, liquidation preferences, and specific dividend reset mechanics.
